scenario: Scenario 1: Purge drops a restarted JN's open segment, so acked txns are forgotten
notes: Chain for MC-1 (Scenario 1; spec/output/hunt/gated/purge_guided_b_bfs.out, 69 states, found by BFS of MC_hunt_purge_restart.cfg under the pruning-only constraints GuideScenario1 and GuideAllUp, so it is also a violation of that cfg): with three JournalNodes, writer w1 commits txn 1 and sends txn 2 while a checkpoint purgeLogsOlderThan(1) fans out to every channel; j0 and j1 ack txn 2 and j0 crashes, and w1's purge task for j0 binds committedTxId 1 before w1 sees the quorum for txn 2, then waits in IPC connect retries; w1 commits txn 2 (j1 learns C = 2 from its purge), j0 restarts with FileJournalManager.currentInProgress null, w1 stops, and the retried purge stale-marks j0's open segment [1,2], so j0 forgets the txn 2 it acknowledged; w2 recovers with j0 (no segment, C = 1) and the lagging j2 ([1,1], C = 1) as its prepare quorum, decides [1,1], passes the client-side committedTxId check, and its acceptRecovery([1,1]) at j1 (current [1,2], committedTxnId 2) fails the guard because 2 is in [1,2] but not in [1,1]. The trigger needs a JournalNode crash and restart within the connect-retry window (RESTART) and a specific order of the purge, the commit and a slow j1 outside the prepare quorum (INTERLEAVING), hence COMBINED. Phase 4a reproduced it on the pristine base commit 734dd8a67cd with a variant of the workload test (repro/test_bugMC-1_purge_restart.java, run by repro/test_bugMC-1_purge_restart.sh) that uses the public QJM API, one MiniJournalCluster JournalNode stop and restart, per-channel task-start delays from an existing test hook and the production-default connect retries: the target fired in 6 of 6 final runs (3 with -ea, 3 without) and 12 of 12 earlier runs, in the counterexample order and in a purge-after-crash order, while a control with the purge delivered before the crash kept txids [1, 2]; with assertions off the failover completed and the quorum served only txid [1], so the acknowledged txn 2 was lost (confirmation/MC-1/logs/transcript-da-run1.txt). The frame reads Journal.java:932 rather than 926 because the throw statement starts at line 926 and javap maps new AssertionError (pc 295) to line 926 but the constructor call (pc 324) to line 932 (harness/logs/target_frame_javap.txt); the throw is unconditional, so it fires with or without -ea. A second, independent path is also confirmed: MC-4 (late accept, not a brief Scenario; found by the Phase 2 sanity check and hunted with MC_hunt_late_accept.cfg; spec/output/hunt/late_accept_bfs.out, 73 states, with the canonical sequential-failover trace spec/output/hunt/gated/late_accept_seq_bfs.out), where a slow JournalNode's queued acceptRecovery binds the new writer's committedTxId from the next segment during a fault-free failover (INTERLEAVING, no counted fault); it fired with the same frame in 4 of 4 runs of repro/test_bugMC-4_late_accept.java (repro/test_bugMC-4_late_accept.out and repro/test_bugMC-4_late_accept.repeat.log). Scenario 2 (epoch-ranked decision across re-incarnated segments, MC_hunt_reincarnation.cfg) and Scenario 3 (half-done accept and unvalidated download, MC_hunt_halfaccept.cfg) found no violation within their bounds, although TargetReached probes show both bounds reach the guard's code path (spec/output/hunt/probes/reach_reincarnation_sim.out, depth 78; spec/output/hunt/probes/reach_halfaccept_sim.out, depth 77); Phase 4a judged the matching code-review entries CR-2 (repro/test_bugCR-2_reincarnated_segment_stale_copy.sh) and CR-3 (repro/test_bugCR-3_halfdone_accept_download.java) FALSE POSITIVE. Rows with NO_VIOLATION_INCOMPLETE stopped at the 30-minute cap: BFS rows give the distinct states and level of the last Progress line and the seconds from Starting to that line; simulation rows (depth 100) give states checked and traces generated, with diameter null and seconds equal to the cap. Outside the hunts, the fault-free MC.cfg (recovery calls filtered with RecoveryCallsCarryNoC = TRUE) checked TargetSafe without violation (1,335,108 distinct states, diameter 92, spec/output/convergence/MC_round1.out), the Phase 2 guided smoke run of MC_hunt_purge_restart.cfg with GuideScenario1 also violated TargetSafe at depth 69 (26,112,745 distinct states, 28 min 21 s, spec/output/guided_purge_restart/guided_tlc_summary.log), and all 3 traces (the workload and two variants) passed trace validation (spec/output/trace_validation/round1/).
